title: Make in India in defence
summary: Structure and facts for a three-minute talk on defence self-reliance.
body: For years India was among the world's largest arms importers. Self-reliance in defence is now a national priority.
Positive indigenisation lists bar imports of hundreds of items; a large share of the capital budget is reserved for domestic industry; defence industrial corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Tejas light combat aircraft, INS Vikrant, the Pinaka rocket system, Akash and BrahMos missiles, and Navy-designed warships such as the Next Generation Corvettes ordered in 2026.
Engines and some electronics are still imported; long development times; the private sector needs a larger role.
Self-reliance is not isolation: it means India can fight with what it builds.
